title: Stationary cue placement and native size shape global activity-vector reorientation
role: One stationary localized-cue experiment; global complex activity-vector definition, systematic native-rate comparison and selected local-field illustration.
legend:
**Figure 3. Stationary cue placement and native size shape global activity-vector reorientation.** Four native periodic models are challenged from exact qualified polarized basals, using chemical circumferences 30/35/40 and Spring resting circumferences 2.5/2.75/3. Stationary localized cues preserve native kinetics, input channels, coefficients and physical supports. Initial physical centre arc d₀ is prescribed from the preparation axis; all internal and overlapping placements remain. The completed experiment contains 645 protocols: 175 exact archive-pair reuses and 470 fresh branches.

**A, Measured vector construction.** Local active concentration is a real scalar. Weighting each physical active amount by its outward unit normal gives two Cartesian components, represented together by the complex first moment $M_1=C\langle u e^{2\pi iq}\rangle$. Normalization $P=M_1/M_1(0)$ rotates the reference axes once and sets $P(0)=1$; $R=|P|$. Actual Holmes C=30 profiles before and after a 300-unit cue at d₀=14 show how directional contributions partly cancel. Blue arrows are exact normalized native-cell sums in twelve 30° sectors, translated for display; red is their sum, with one shared vector scale. Active amount rises to 1.029 of baseline while R falls to 0.259. Colours share a zero-based native concentration scale; orange arcs mark cue supports. This is a cue-on state, without a stationary-fate or site-ancestry inference. Its later cue-free field tail fails the finite gate.

**B, Complete placement comparison.** Early instantaneous native-RHS angular rate at native time 10 is shown for all 129 placements using their 1000-unit cue branches. Colour identifies native size, with chemical C/Spring C₀ pairs in the shared key. Circles, diamonds and triangles classify complete initial footprints inside, straddling or outside the interpolated 10%-contrast region. Lines connect tested points without fitting a distance law. All 129 displayed instants retain full-state/snapshot support and R≥0.1. Nonmonotone distance profiles and changing size ranks demonstrate why global angular rate requires spatial context. Full temporal and duration responses remain in the supplement.

**C, Native field history and resultant.** Wave-pinning C=30/40 basals receive the same fully external cue at d₀=11 for 1000 units. Every saved field uses common physical-arc and native-amplitude scales; grey padding is outside the shorter domain. Dashed lines mark initial 10%-contrast edges; white lines/orange bars mark cue centres/supports. Time is linear through 0.1 then logarithmic. Equal-scale complex-P paths retain direction and magnitude; the circle is R=1, squares mark withdrawal and numbers give actual native times. Dotted rays mark actual targets. Targets differ (132°/99°), so architecture and angular geometry change together.

Rates describe an activity resultant rather than peak or cell velocity. Initial projection and moment magnitude matter; cross-model clocks are uncalibrated. Complete duration grids, definitions, weak-vector masking, all 645 outcomes, native profiles and finite 13,000-unit cue-free tail qualifications are reported in the comprehensive supplement; no causal geometry partition or asymptotic-stability claim follows.
narrative: Scalar local activity adds directionally to a complex first moment; nearly retained active amount can accompany a small resultant.
Global cue-on angular rate varies nonmonotonically with prescribed physical distance, and native size ordering can change across distance.
Initial geometric projection, evolving moment magnitude and native organization must be considered alongside rate; no intrinsic local remodeling speed is identified.
measurements: 645 requested and complete: 175 exact reuses + 470 fresh branches; 129 initial placements; 12 qualified basals
All 129 onset/time 10 native-RHS anchors; 4740 full-state rates in the clean 12-condition support
All 645 withdrawal and finite endpoint moments; 124086 actual saved secant intervals; 11610 regional-entry records
620 passing, 8 failing and 17 unavailable finite field tails; all nine two-region Holmes endpoints retain those limitations
limitations: Matching initial physical arc changes angular target and native basal architecture; no causal geometry partition.
R<0.1 masks phase/rate; near-antipodal changes require magnitude and native fields.
Cue-free endpoints are finite 13000-unit readouts, not proof of asymptotic coexistence.
Operational edge/footprint classes do not identify internal causal pathways or site ancestry.
